headline: Math is nearly solved; agents doing real work remain the gap
outlook: Math is where the field has moved fastest, closing about 95% of its remaining headroom over the past year: FrontierMath, its Tier 4 set and ARC-AGI-2 have all crossed 90% since June, and GPT-6.1 Sol posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4 in late September. Agents doing real work are moving more slowly, closing only about a third of their headroom. GPT-6 Astra's 20.8% on the Remote Labor Index and Claude Opus 5's 31.4% on OSWorld 2 put 90% no earlier than 2027 on current trends, even though APEX-Agents jumped from 68.6% to 82.2% across three records in eight days in September. Meanwhile, the length of task models can handle is doubling roughly every 4.1 months and now stands at 17.4 hours with Claude Mythos Preview, which on current trends makes a full 40-hour work-week most likely around December, though the range stretches to August 2027. Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are running behind their fits despite being close to 90%, and past forecast ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, so the next year looks like cheaper, stronger reasoning (GPQA-level performance has fallen from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens) alongside an open question about how quickly longer task horizons turn into reliable real-world work.
